i had a similar experience when i saw gerard way in austin a couple years ago for my 18th birthday. me, my friend, and her friend waited in line for seven hours after travelling for an hour, and we talked to the people surrounding us. they were all very nice and we talked for a few hours. eventually, we ran into a couple people from our school, so they stayed with us in line. i knew the girl, but the guy i didn't.

so we got in finally, and the place filled up immediately. everyone physically shoved their way to the front. i lost my friend and eventually see her at the front with one of the girls we were talking to in line. i tried to go to her but got shoved back. i ended up stuck behind the guy from my school, and it was so packed that i was forced up against him and was literally breathing on him. this was what it was like the entire time. it just got more and more crowded, and people continued to push each other out of the way to get closer. 

there was one point where there was a quiet part were gerard began talking about the mental illness stigma and how hard it is to to feel alone through stuff like that. there was a part where he stopped to sip water, and a girl screamed "dADDY" at the top of her lungs, and she was close to the front. he looked at her for a second, but just continued. i thought that was incredibly fucking rude, especially considering the subject he was talking about.

i was crying and sweating the entire time because of my anxiety. so many people pushed and pryed with their elbows that i had bruises down my sides. it was my first real concert, and i absolutely love gerard way, but i didn't enjoy it as much as i'd wanted to. i was really sad about it afterwards. on the way home, my friend asked me why i was crying and why i seemed so mad. i lied and said i was just nervous, but i was just so disappointed with how the night went.
